analysis: The 32-to-8 hard-negative mining trial completed successfully but did not improve validation macro HR@10: the host measured 0.5700 versus the reported prior 0.5737, a decrease of 0.0037. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.600, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.605, Electronics 0.430, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.645. Electronics had the lowest absolute score; prior category scores were not supplied, so the regression cannot be attributed to a category. These results do not support replacing eight uniform negatives with this mining configuration. Hard-negative selection changes the sampled training objective and may emphasize difficult or false-negative items, but the supplied evidence does not establish the cause. Allocated GPU time was 265.52 seconds.
code_summary: Trains one independent GRURec model per category from seed 42. Each model uses 96-dimensional tied normalized item embeddings, input LayerNorm, a two-layer GRU, dropout 0.25, and a linear/LayerNorm projection with normalized output states. Scores combine scaled cosine similarity with jointly learned item bias. For each valid position, training samples 32 uniform candidate IDs excluding the positive, selects the eight highest detached model scores, and recomputes their logits with gradients. The loss retains separate positive and negative softplus means; mining uses chunks of 1024 positions. AdamW, gradient clipping, AMP, and validation-based checkpoint selection remain. The generated predictor routes among all four categories and strictly loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category, preserving right-padding and truncation. No ensemble or separately fitted auxiliary scorer is used.
